### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **53** documentable anchor(s).

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cc14657ede79cd315fa7647da238a48a6ede9b88`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/meta (route, 39 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cc14657ede79cd315fa7647da238a48a6ede9b88` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `331090103361bafd953635e533a457f0fe955534` — the merge of head `dbe63f841ec091d52db73a5d048e4ab0b3b1a228` into base `cc14657ede79cd315fa7647da238a48a6ede9b88`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 331090103361bafd953635e533a457f0fe955534 && git checkout 331090103361bafd953635e533a457f0fe955534
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cc14657ede79cd315fa7647da238a48a6ede9b88 dbe63f841ec091d52db73a5d048e4ab0b3b1a228 && git checkout -B drift-repro cc14657ede79cd315fa7647da238a48a6ede9b88 && git merge --no-ff dbe63f841ec091d52db73a5d048e4ab0b3b1a228

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cc14657ede79cd315fa7647da238a48a6ede9b88
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cc14657ede79cd315fa7647da238a48a6ede9b88` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dbe63f841ec091d52db73a5d048e4ab0b3b1a228`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23231 (body and all six comments: ruling 6145019463, claim 6148875683, shared-pages note 6149658350, dev reports 6154188969 and 6155532025, seat direction 6154226716), PR #23330 (body, the 31-file list, the net diff against its merge base), the head's check-runs (41 names; latest run per name: 34 success, 7 skipped, 0 other, `Check Changeset` included), and the head tree read through `git show`. Rules read: `contract-review.md`, the Clause-② lines of `execution-duties.md`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, ADR-0131 (D3, D11, D12 items 7–8), ADR-0087 (D3 and the disposition addendum). Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named and judged:

1. **`walledCatalogWriteVerdict` (`@objectstack/metadata-core`, a published export): runtime accept set narrows.** The first line `if (!isSecurityCatalogType(input.type)) return { allowed: true }` is gone; under `group` and `isolated` a caller that is neither `isSystem` nor the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung is refused for every `type`. The TypeScript signature is byte-identical (the same four input fields, the same `MetaWriteCapabilityVerdict` return), so nothing on the type surface widens. Absent posture and `single` stay inert. **Right** — this is ruling A on #23231 and ADR-0131 D12 items 7–8 ("plants assign; plants do not define … or any metadata") read through D11 (identical rules, only the wall differs); D3's catalog clause was the first case and is subsumed, not reversed.
2. **`isSecurityCatalogType`, `SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES`, `PLATFORM_OPERATOR_POSTURE`: kept, semantics unchanged.** At the head no non-test caller in `packages/` uses the metadata-core predicate as a pre-filter any more (the surviving `isSecurityCatalogType` hits are objectql's own symbol of that name and core's catalog module). **Right** — keeping the exports avoids a `runtime-export-retired` move on symbols the W-family changelogs advertise; the docblock now says the predicate decides no refusal.
3. **REST `/meta` save, reset, publish, rollback (`walledCatalogRefusal`): pre-filter removed, `403 FORBIDDEN` for every type.** Five `this.walledCatalogRefusal(` call sites at the head: the four item doors plus `_migrate-stored`. **Right** — each asks after `metaSaveVerdict`'s capability gate and before `resolveProtocol`.
4. **Dispatcher `PUT /meta/:type/:name`: the `if (isSecurityCatalogType(type))` wrapper removed, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` for every type.** **Right** — same predicate, the transport's own envelope, pinned with `isSystem`, operator and `single` controls.
5. **`POST /meta/_migrate-stored`, both transports, preview and apply alike.** Verdict with `type: 'sys_metadata'`, after the capability gate and before the protocol is resolved or a row is read; the subject key is a private map entry, not an export. **Right** — seat direction 6154226716 §2 (option A, in this PR) and the ruling's rule, whose door list enumerates and does not bound. Refusing the preview is judged right too: the ruling's rule is per door, the preview is the same operator tool over the same install-wide ledger, and a door-level gate that refuses before parsing the body is the fail-closed shape; the changeset, the semantic entry and `api/metadata-api.mdx` all declare "preview included", so the claim is as wide as the enforcement and no wider.
6. **All thirteen `/packages` write doors (`refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite`): asked right after `requireManageMetadata`, before any read or write; `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`.** Thirteen call sites at the head (create, manifest `PATCH`, enable, disable, publish, publish-drafts, discard-drafts, revert, rollback, `commits/:commitId/revert`, duplicate, adopt-orphans, delete); the `readTypes` parameter and the three item readers (`storedRowTypes`, `readCommitRow`, `commitItemTypes`) are deleted, so the W3 500-on-read path is gone with them; `rollback` and `duplicate` now refuse before their body check and `requireDuplicableSource`. The function is module-local, not a runtime export. **Right** — the ruling names "the `/packages` write actions" and no catalog pre-filter is left.
7. **`install-local` install, upgrade, uninstall (`refuseWalledCatalogPackage`): the manifests parameter and the objectql catalog reading are gone; `403 FORBIDDEN` with `type: 'package'`.** The refusal's `error.details` shrinks from `{ manifestId, catalogItems }` to `{ manifestId }` — a response-shape narrowing on a refusal envelope, declared in the changeset's FROM → TO; at the head `catalogItems` survives only in shipped CHANGELOG prose, in no spec contract, client type or doc page. The method is a private member of the exported `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin`, so the `.d.ts` surface does not move. **Right.**
8. **`/automation` create, update, delete, clone (new module-local `refuseWalledFlowDefinitionWrite`, `type: 'flow'`): `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` after the capability gate, before the service; the enablement door is left to the ADR-0126 §5 activation gate.** Not named by the ruling, but measured open (200, and B read A's flow) and inside the ruling's rule by the same reading the seat gave `_migrate-stored`. **Right** — leaving it open would have made the PR's own claim false.
9. **Activation remedies (`FLOW_ACTIVATION_SUBJECT`, `ACTION_ACTIVATION_SUBJECT`, `PERMISSION_SET_ACTIVATION_SUBJECT`): remedy strings now name the operator, never a clone or a sibling item.** `activation-gate.ts` is not re-exported from the runtime index; these are runtime message strings. **Right** — that refusal is answered only under a wall, where the clone and author doors now refuse the same caller; a remedy recommending them would advertise a door that refuses the reader (Prime Directive #10). The platform-checklist clause that quoted the action remedy is corrected in the same diff.
10. **Error codes: none new.** `FORBIDDEN` and `PERMISSION_DENIED` pre-exist in `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`; the "a new code is always `yes`" rule does not fire.
11. **`@objectstack/spec`: one new ADR-0087 semantic entry `walled-environment-metadata-writes-retired`; the W2 and W3 entries' `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` corrected.** Entries are enumerated from the `entries/semantic/` directory (`gen:migration-registry`, `migrations.test.ts`), so no hand index is owed. A registry element is data on the published `./migrations` subpath, not a type or an accept set, so it widens nothing. The W2/W3 edits remove the sentence "a package with no catalog item is handled exactly as before", which this diff falsifies, and point at the new entry. **Right** — the ledger stays true to the chain it describes.
12. **ADR anchor `packages__metadata-core__src__meta-write-capability.ts.json`: invariant rewritten to "every environment-metadata type … no door pre-filters on the written type".** Matches the code at the head. **Right.**
13. **Doors not edited.** The security plugin's data door (`walled-catalog-data-door.ts`) still maps only the three catalog row objects before asking the verdict: that is a filter on which *data* objects reach it, not a catalog pre-filter on a metadata-type door, it is not a door the ruling names, and the objects it guards retired at stage 8. The permission-set clone door asks the verdict with its fixed type. Not in scope, correctly left alone.
14. **Prose surfaces** (`content/docs/**` five pages, the changeset body, the checklist clause) are outside this review's three surfaces and are ACCEPT's; read for consistency with items 1–9: consistent, including the `install-local` envelope and the `single` row.

The PR body's sentence "`check:api-surface` is green" names the spec-scoped gate in `lint.yml` (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:api-surface`); it is evidence for `@objectstack/spec` only. The evidence for the other four packages is items 1, 6, 7 and 9 above: no index file is in the file list and no exported signature moves.

### ② Semver level

- **Clause-② line.** The claim (6148875683), the PR body and the changeset all carry the value `no (narrowing)`. The ruling's workload column wrote `yes (narrowing)`, which in `clause2-line.mjs` is "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another". This diff widens nothing (① items 1, 2, 7, 10, 11): no new export, no new error code, no new response field, no new authorable key. So `no (narrowing)` is the measured value and `yes (narrowing)` would have been a false `yes`; the ruling's substance — one contract-review-tier review before the queue — is this record. The claim argued the point in writing against the ruling, as it should.
- **Changeset `.changeset/23231-walled-environment-metadata-writes.md`.** Bumps `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/spec` at `minor` — the five published packages whose source the diff moves. Correct level: an accept-set narrowing is breaking, and under the launch-window convention (ADR-0087 amendment of 2026-09-13, enforced by `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`; `.changeset/pre.json` is present) a breaking change ships `minor` with the banner and the disposition as the carriers.
- **BREAKING banner.** Present: `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing, shipped as minor …`, plus the `!` in the title; `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads both and the `narrowing` arm as declarations of breaking-ness, and the disposition it then demands is present: `adr-0087: registered walled-environment-metadata-writes-retired`, an id that resolves at the head and is new in this diff.
- **ADR-0087 semantic entries match what the diff publishes.** The new entry's `surface` names exactly the doors of ① items 3–8 (REST `/meta` four verbs, dispatcher `PUT`, `_migrate-stored` on both transports preview included, the thirteen `/packages` verbs, `install-local` POST and DELETE, the four `/automation` definition writes); its `replacement` names the operator rung and the custom-door rule; its `acceptanceCriteria` are the dogfood pins' own readings. The W2/W3 entries no longer promise the catalog-free path this diff closes. The FROM → TO list in the changeset matches the entry door for door, and names the `catalogItems` removal.
- `Check Changeset`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on this head, which is where the two gates above run.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated:

1. **Open question (6154188969): wall `_migrate-stored` too?** Answered by seat direction 6154226716 §2 (A, in this PR), executed in patch round 1 and verified in the diff (① item 5). Closed. The second report carries `open_questions: []`.
2. **File surface grew beyond the claim** (`automation.ts`, `activation-gate.ts`, the W2/W3 entries, `tenancy-modes.mdx`, the checklist clause). Answered: each is a measured reach or a sentence this diff falsified; same defect class, same gate family, no new rule. Accepted (① items 8, 9, 11, 14).
3. **Preview of `_migrate-stored` refused too** (6155532025 deviation 1). Answered right in ① item 5; declared in the changeset, the entry and the docs.
4. **Changeset's "Unchanged" clause on `_migrate-stored` deleted; census row 55b and the ADR anchor name the door** (deviations 2–3). Answered: all three registers now say what the code does; `check:system-context-census` and `check:adr-anchors` are inside the green lint runs.
5. **PR body edits the seat owed after round 1.** Verified present on the PR: the `_migrate-stored` row in the BEFORE table, its entry under "What changed", the dropped "Not walled here" note, the round-1 pins and ablation leg 3 under "Tests".
6. **Fork clause (HQ IT).** Reported on the card as the ruling required (6154188969; restated in 6154226716 §1), written into `deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx`: a stock `group` deployment's HQ IT is the operator and keeps authoring; an HQ IT holding only an organization-scoped set must be declared in `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`. Per the ruling, "not a reason to keep the hole" — no block from this record; the seat's round report carries it to the maintainer.
7. **Ablation no-op redone; four commands backgrounded; the gate battery straddling two commits; the step-1 harness never committed** (6154188969 deviations 2–4, 6; 6155532025 deviation 4). Procedural, with no effect on the diff; the committed dogfood file carries the BEFORE/AFTER pins, and the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts this record reads.
8. **Commit trailers model-free** (deviation 5). Consistent with AGENTS.md; no model identifier is in the diff, the PR body or this record.
9. **`check:platform-checklist` exits 1 on `origin/main` with 8 ABSENT SYMBOL problems, none in this diff** — "noted, not filed". **Escalated to the dispatching seat:** `lint.yml` keeps that gate out of per-PR CI by maintainer decision (it is a hand-run gate), so it is not a verdict on this head and not a FAIL here; but a red on `main` that reproduces is a reproducible defect under Prime Directive #10, and seat direction 6154226716 §3 already owns the ACCEPT reading of it — the seat files the card if the reading holds.
10. **`@objectstack/cloud-connection` keeps the `@objectstack/objectql` dependency W2 added, now unimported.** Not a contract matter; carried in the PR's Acceptance notes, which is where Prime Directive #10 puts it. Answered.
11. **The names keep "catalog" although they judge every type.** Answered: a rename would retire exports that seat 2's `walled-catalog-data-door.ts` reads under those names (a `runtime-export-retired` move on another lane's region); the docblocks say why the name stays. A later card, when seat 2's lane allows.
12. **`walled-catalog-data-door.ts` vestigial after stage 8.** Seat 2's region (#22975), not this PR's; carried as a note to that lane. Not escalated further here.
13. **Shared-pages note (6149658350, `domain:devx`).** This PR edits `permission-sets.mdx` and `system-context.mdx`, two of the four pages #22976 will touch; #22976 is not dispatched. The note's own rule governs: whichever lands later merges `main` and re-reads the other's sentences. Nothing owed before landing.
14. **Docs Drift Check (PR comment 6154005622).** Advisory and precision-first; the five content pages this diff edits are the ones its anchors reach through the walled doors; the rest is ACCEPT's prose reading.
